proofs.text: Run `scan()` against a repository with one feature and one passing record; verify the text opens `Purlin: <project>, gate strong`, counts `1 features, 2 rules.`, carries a line per bucket the gate reaches, and names the newest record with its path, the source `developer` and its timestamp. Run it against a repository with no record; verify the line `No record has been committed yet.`. Render a rollup whose summary counts one rule in every bucket plus 1 stale, 1 held and 2 needing a person; verify every bucket name is printed with `1 signatures stale` and `2 rules need a person`

rule_text: The rollup names the project, the gate, how many of the rules meet it beside how many are failing, and one line per bucket the gate reaches, then the newest record with its path, source and timestamp, or says no record has been committed yet

tests.name: test_the_newest_record_is_the_one_with_the_latest_timestamp

tests.body:
def test_the_rollup_names_the_newest_record_and_its_label(remote):
    bare, source = remote
    head = git(source, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD').stdout.strip()
    rel = add_record(source, head)
    git(source, 'push', '--quiet')

    text = scan_module.scan(bare, 'main')

    assert rel in text
    assert 'developer' in text, 'the label a person\'s commit earns'
    assert '0 commits behind the latest record.' in text
tests.name: test_the_rollup_names_the_newest_record_and_its_label
test_every_bucket_the_package_names_can_be_printed

def test_the_rollup_names_the_project_the_gate_and_the_buckets(remote):
    bare, _source = remote
    text = scan_module.scan(bare, 'main')

    assert 'gate strong' in text
    assert '1 features, 2 rules.' in text
    assert 'untested' in text, 'no bucket was counted'
    assert 'No record has been committed yet.' in text
